title: Introduction
summary: This page introduces the protocol’s original stETH-backed borrowing model, the role of boxETH, yield-linked position incentives, and the limited administrative controls described at publication.

title: Use Cases
summary: The article surveys ways the project expected users to supply collateral, borrow boxETH, participate in liquidity or fee-token activity, and resolve debt positions.

title: User Guide
summary: This guide walks through the project’s documented user workflows for collateral deposits, borrowing and repayment, managing position health, third-party resolution, and fee-token participation.

title: Components
summary: The page describes the protocol’s main components, including borrower positions, the peg-stability module, resolution activity, and fee-token staking, with diagrams on the original site.

title: Asset Valuations
summary: This short article discusses how a user might reason about the value of boxETH in particular transaction histories. It is project documentation, not tax advice or a live market quote.

title: Contracts
summary: The published page lists protocol contract addresses and identifies their broad roles. Confirm an address and its current code before interacting with it.

title: Approvals
summary: This page outlines token allowances the original interface expects for selected protocol operations, including collateral, debt repayment, and fee-token staking.

title: Admin Controls
summary: The article describes the project’s published view of administrative controls and its then-current plans for managing protocol fees and automated market operations.

title: Resolve
summary: This guide presents a resolver workflow based on tracking borrower activity, inspecting a position’s terms, comparing a market purchase with the resolution cost, and submitting a resolution transaction. Verify view names, fee tokens, and limits against deployed contracts.

title: boxFEE Tokenomics
summary: The page discusses the original boxFEE distribution narrative, staking, backing, liquidity plans, and possible holder exit paths. Treat market and backing statements as historical project claims.

title: Version 1.1
summary: This release note compares documented v1 and v1.1 behavior, including the project’s descriptions of position incentives, borrowing fees, and fee-token routing.

title: Explainer Video
summary: The original page contains an embedded project explainer video.

title: Teaser Video
summary: The original page contains an embedded project teaser video.
